# link-image-style

- ID: `MD054`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `images`, `links`

Links and images use only the allowed styles. By default, all are allowed.

## Why

A project may prefer one way of writing links. Autolinks show raw URLs, inline
links take room in the source, and reference links need a definition elsewhere.

## Options

Set them under `rules.link-image-style.options`.

- `autolink` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow autolinks, such as
  \<https\://example.com\>.
- `inline` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow inline links and images, such as
  \[text\](url).
- `full` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow full reference links and images,
  such as \[text\]\[label\].
- `collapsed` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow collapsed reference links and
  images, such as \[label\]\[\].
- `shortcut` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow shortcut reference links and
  images, such as \[label\].
- `url_inline` (`boolean`, default `true`): Allow inline links whose text is
  their URL, such as \[https\://example.com\](https\://example.com).

## Fix

There is no automatic fix.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  link-image-style:
    options:
      autolink: true
```

Under `rules`, `link-image-style: false` turns the rule off and
`link-image-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable link-image-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line link-image-style -->
```
